content:
Ready for a full Class 6 Maths Olympiad rehearsal? A real IMO or SOF paper mixes every chapter — numbers, integers, fractions, decimals, algebra, ratio, geometry, symmetry, mensuration, data handling and logical reasoning — in one paper. This free test gives a 10-question taste, and the practice-papers e-book gives you 25 complete Maths Olympiad Class 6 sample papers with answers.

What a Class 6 IMO sample paper looks like

  • 30 questions in one paper, balanced across all 14 chapters
  • A mix of number work, algebra, ratio, geometry, mensuration, data handling and reasoning
  • An answer key and step-by-step solution for every question
  • Graded intermediate to hard, just like the real SOF Olympiad

How to use Class 6 Olympiad practice papers

  • Sit one paper in a quiet 30–40 minute slot, no help
  • Mark it with the answer key, then read the solution for every wrong one
  • Note which chapter the mistakes cluster in and revise that chapter
  • Repeat weekly — steady practice beats last-minute cramming

Take the free mixed test

The 10 questions below are pulled from across the syllabus. The full 25 Practice Papers e-book has 750 questions — 25 papers of 30 — each fully solved, with colourful diagrams wherever they help: the best Maths Olympiad class 6 question papers PDF for exam practice.

Learn the syllabus first with the free IMO Maths Olympiad course at vidaara.org.

questions.q: In the number 3,70,825, what is the place value of the digit 3 in the lakhs place?
questions.explanation: The digit 3 is in the lakhs place, so its place value = 3 x 1,00,000 = 3,00,000.

questions.q: Is 143 a prime number or a composite number?
If the shadow of a 6 m pole is 4 m long, find the shadow of a 15 m tree at the same time.
In a triangle, the sum of any two sides is always greater than the what?
questions.explanation: Triangle inequality: sum of two sides > third side.
